name: Khatu Shyam Temple

mythology: Khatu Shyam of Rajasthan is worshipped as a form of Krishna–Barbarika (son of Ghatotkacha) in popular Mahabharata-linked devotion. Folklore holds that Krishna granted Barbarika worship in Kaliyuga under the name Shyam — making Khatu a living bridge between epic memory and folk Vaishnavism.

mythologySignificance:
Khatu Shyam of Rajasthan is worshipped as a form of Krishna–Barbarika (son of Ghatotkacha) in popular Mahabharata-linked devotion. Folklore holds that Krishna granted Barbarika worship in Kaliyuga under the name Shyam — making Khatu a living bridge between epic memory and folk Vaishnavism.

Pilgrimage literature treats Khatu Shyam Temple as a tirtha — a crossing where devotion to Shyam Baba (Barbarika tradition) is believed to bear fruit more readily than in ordinary space. Accounts summarised here follow widely cited epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya traditions; temple priests remain the guides for ritual detail.
localBeliefs:
Phalguna Mela transforms the small town into one of Rajasthan’s densest pilgrimages. Devotees offer coconuts, chadars, and songs, believing Shyam Baba removes impossible obstacles.

‘Shyam baba ki jai’ processions and village-to-temple walking vows are the heartbeat of local faith.
